unit.title: Branch: World Cup and national teams

lessons.title: The 48-team format
lessons.objective: You can explain groups, best third-placed teams and the round of 32.

payload.prompt: The 2026 World Cup has 48 teams split into groups. How many teams are in each group?

explanation.correct: Right. Twelve groups of four make 48 teams. The top two advance, plus the eight best third-placed teams.
explanation.incorrect: The 2026 World Cup has twelve groups of four, so 12 x 4 = 48 teams. The top two from each group advance, plus eight third-placed teams.
explanation.sayThisLine: Twelve groups of four, that's the new format.

payload.prompt: Complete the 2026 World Cup knockout qualification.
payload.template: The top {{top}} teams from each group plus the {{best}} best third-placed teams make up the {{total}} teams in the round of 32.

explanation.correct: Right. Two from each of 12 groups (24) plus the 8 best third-place teams = 32 knockouts.
explanation.incorrect: In the 48-team format, the top two from every group advance, plus the eight best third-place finishers. That totals 32 teams for the round of 32.

payload.prompt: Guess: how many group games does each team play?

explanation.correct: Right. In a four-team group, each team plays the other three once, so three matches per team.
explanation.incorrect: With four teams in a group and each playing everyone else once, that's 3 matches per team (4 teams − 1 opponent = 3 matches).
explanation.sayThisLine: Three matches to get out of your group, make them count.

payload.prompt: Is 2026 the first World Cup to feature 48 teams instead of 32?

scene.alt: A stadium with flags from many nations gathered for the World Cup.

explanation.correct: True. The World Cup had 32 teams from 1998 to 2022. The 2026 expansion to 48 is a historic first.
explanation.incorrect: 2026 is the first World Cup with 48 teams. Every tournament from 1998 to 2022 had 32.
explanation.sayThisLine: Forty-eight teams changes the whole tournament structure.

lessons.title: National teams vs clubs
lessons.objective: You can explain qualifiers, breaks and how national teams differ from clubs.

payload.prompt: What is an international break in the club calendar?

options.text: A pause in club matches so players can play for their national teams in qualifiers or tournaments
A transfer window where clubs stop playing and sign new players
An off-season where all football stops

explanation.correct: Exactly. International breaks stop the club season so national teams can play. Players leave their clubs to represent their country.
explanation.incorrect: An international break pauses club fixtures to allow players to join their national teams for qualifying matches or tournament games.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: She plays for a club but she still dreams about the World Cup with her national team.

payload.question: What does this tell you about how players value the two competitions?

options.text: Club football is more important because it pays better
Playing for your country at the World Cup is a lifelong dream, separate from club glory
International football is less competitive than club football
National team football carries special meaning and pride beyond club trophies

payload.translation: Players can be proud of their club career and still feel a deep pull toward World Cup glory. National team duty is a separate honor and dream from club success.

followUps.line: What's your country's record in World Cups?
Would she skip a club trophy for World Cup glory?
followUps.why: Shows you understand the emotional weight.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: It's fine to ask which national teams have won the most World Cups; that's a real question.

payload.prompt: Match the tournament or event to how it fits into a player's calendar.

pairs.definition: Club play pauses so national teams can play matches that determine who reaches the World Cup tournament.
A scheduled pause in the club league season so players can join their national teams for matches.
The global championship where national teams compete for the world title.

explanation.summary: Qualifying determines who goes to the World Cup; the international break accommodates national team duties; the tournament itself is the ultimate stage.
explanation.sayThisLine: International football has qualifiers, breaks and finally the World Cup.

payload.prompt: The three 2026 hosts had to win qualifying like everyone else. True or false?

scene.alt: Flags of the United States, Canada and Mexico together above a World Cup trophy.

explanation.correct: False. Hosts qualify automatically, so the USA, Canada and Mexico were in the 48-team field without going through qualifying.
explanation.incorrect: Host nations are given automatic places. The USA, Canada and Mexico did not have to go through qualifying for 2026.

lessons.title: Talking about 2026
lessons.objective: You can talk about Spain, Argentina and the tournament highlights.

payload.prompt: What happened in the 2026 World Cup final?

options.text: Argentina won in a penalty shootout
Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time when Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute

explanation.correct: Yes. Spain won 1-0 with a goal in extra time, a dramatic ending to a tense final.
explanation.incorrect: Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in the 2026 World Cup final after extra time. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute.

statement.speaker: Jamie
statement.text: World Cup wins matter so much when people rank the all-time greats.

payload.question: What is Jamie saying about how we judge player legacies?

options.text: Club trophies are the only measure of greatness
World Cup success weighs heavily when deciding who the GOAT (Greatest Of All Time) is
Only players who win multiple World Cups can be called great
The GOAT debate compares players partly on international tournament success

payload.translation: One major factor fans use when debating the greatest player ever is whether they won the World Cup and how they performed in it. It's one piece of the GOAT argument.

followUps.line: How many World Cups has your favorite player won?
Do you think club trophies matter more or less than World Cups?
followUps.why: Invites her take on the debate.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: It's okay to say you've heard people argue about who the GOAT is; everyone does.

payload.title: The 2026 World Cup
payload.setting: She is reminiscing about the 2026 tournament and its dramatic final.

exchanges.theirMessage: Torres in the 106th minute, I'll never forget that moment.

replies.text: That was wild. Were you watching with other people or by yourself?
replies.theirResponse: With my family, we were on the edge of our seats.
replies.coachNote: Shows genuine curiosity about the memory, not just the fact.

replies.text: Yeah, that was the final. Spain won it.

replies.coachNote: Don't dismiss what was special about her moment.

payload.closingNote: She is cherishing a World Cup memory. Ask about where she watched or who was with her, not just facts.

payload.prompt: Spain won the 2026 World Cup final in a penalty shootout. True or false?

scene.alt: A stadium scoreboard showing Spain 1, Argentina 0 after extra time.

explanation.correct: False. There was no shootout. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time, with Ferran Torres scoring in the 106th minute.
explanation.incorrect: Spain won 1-0 after extra time. Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute, so it never reached penalties.
